headline: 本週劇評書評精選
context: 衛報本輪評論橫跨舞台劇、電影與書籍。愛丁堡藝穗節喜劇《The Librarians》嘲諷職場崩壞，致敬經典情境喜劇；動作片《Zip Wire》講一名患強迫症的抗癌科學家，被迫吊在鋼索上對抗殺手；詩人克勞蒂亞・蘭金（Claudia Rankine）新書《Triage》探討面對世界殘酷時該如何自處；娜塔莎・華特（Natasha Walter）新作《Feminism for a World on Fire》則把氣候危機與全球正義運動連在一起。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Pleasance Courtyard, Edinburgh Well-tuned performances help along a familiar set of laughs as a rickety library gets a new manager and an inspection The sign says Plumstanton Library but this could be The Brittas Empire’s Whitbury New Town Leisure Centre, The Office’s Wernham Hogg or Torquay fleapit Fawlty Towers. Such is the instant familiarity of a failing workplace whose staff have a new manager and an inspector to contend with at once. It’s not only the books that are well worn in Matthew Howell and Jack Michael Stacey’s play. Acting head librarian Harry Wordsworth has even bought his own “best boss” mug like David Brent. Nevertheless it’s a frequently funny hour, with well-tuned performances. Harry (Matthew Howell) finds himself in charge when Peter, who has run the library for more than 25 years, pops his clogs in the Agatha Christie section. This death in the aisle is both a tragedy and mystery which the remaining staff stumble through, beset by dodgy electrics, dwindling visitors and a seemingly inevitable closure. At Pleasance Courtyard, Edinburgh , until 31 August All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: This nonsensical film sees an OCD-afflicted scientist fending off assassins while hanging from an aerial wire, and fails to get pulses racing for even a minute In this silly, low-adrenaline thriller, the title star is a rickety old zip wire bolted into the side of a mountain in the Italian Dolomites that was never intended for human use. It was constructed in the first world war to sling weapons and supplies hundreds of feet down the valley – and is still used to get the occasional goat off the mountain. But for the second half of this film, a world-famous British research scientist with an extreme fear of heights dangles from it, fighting off highly skilled assassins in increasingly preposterous ways. The scientist is Amy (MyAnna Buring); she has discovered a cure for lung cancer, and her drive is explained in syrupy hospital-ward flashbacks to her mother dying when she was a teenager. Amy also has OCD – she is so anxious about germs that she never takes off her rubber gloves, and has an assistant in her lab to do anything that involves touching or handling objects. (Like all the characters, she never gets beyond a stereotype.) Her research is bankrolled by a big pharma company, whose CEO is played by Saffron Burrows (now seemingly mandatory casting for ropey British thrillers). Continue reading...
sources.title: Zip Wire review – cancer-curing scientist is on the hook for cable-dangle thriller

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The American poet and essayist weaves memoir, fiction, criticism and lyrical lament into a tale of friendship in an age of existential crisis “Any resemblance to actual persons, living or dead, or actual events is purely coincidental,” writes the multi-award winning Jamaican-American poet, essayist and playwright Claudia Rankine in the disclaimer to her latest work. “Unless it isn’t.” The pretzel-logic of this statement, its assertive ambiguity, sets the tone for a book that digs directly into the question of what we are to do with the idea of truth, when the world we live in is asking us “to hold, visually and emotionally, realities we do not yet have a viable system of language for”. In Triage, Rankine borrows from her personal history and from a world whose landscape now encompasses “the rise of fascism, the implementation through deportations of the Great Replacement theory, the starvation of devastated populations subjected to war and climate change”, and uses the material she gathers to pose a simple question. When faced with realities such as these, what do you do? Do you stand, or do you fall? The book begins with a friendship. Two young people – our narrator, and another she refers to only as “the theorist” – meet in college in the late 20th century, and are drawn to each other. They’re passionate; they’re idealistic; they’re committed to the activism of the time (“shantytowns were built on campus to protest apartheid South Africa”) and steeped in the texts and authors and philosophical conceits of the humanities. Over time, they develop a game. “When we spied each other during the day,” the narrator explains, “we had to collapse.” Continue reading...
sources.title: Triage by Claudia Rankine review – how should we respond to the world’s atrocities?

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A writer and activist links the climate crisis to battles for justice around the world in this vital book It has become increasingly difficult to change our minds, to question our own views or to find common ground with people we disagree with, all of which makes Natasha Walter’s new book both refreshing and exhilarating. In her ebullient 1998 debut The New Feminism, Walter hailed Margaret Thatcher as a trailblazer. In this fiercer, bleaker work, she rips into the “glossy language of aspiration feminism”, “the message that the individual woman can do anything she wants if she only has the necessary courage”. That kind of feminism inspired an “explosion of books and films about pioneers and heroines, about bossy women and gutsy girls” which retold the feminist story as “a succession of isolated campaigns, led by outsize individuals”. Continue reading...
sources.title: Feminism for a World on Fire by Natasha Walter review – hope amid the hopelessness

thread_text: 衛報本輪評論橫跨舞台劇、電影與書籍，題材差很多。愛丁堡藝穗節喜劇《The Librarians》，講一間搖搖欲墜的圖書館迎來新館長與突擊檢查，向經典職場喜劇致敬；動作驚悚片《Zip Wire》裡，一名患強迫症、剛治好肺癌的科學家，被迫吊在懸崖鋼索上對抗殺手；詩人克勞蒂亞・蘭金新書《Triage》探討面對戰爭與氣候危機時，人該如何自處；娜塔莎・華特新作《Feminism for a World on Fire》把氣候危機和全球正義運動連在一起討論。
threads_text: 這輪衛報評論橫跨舞台劇、電影與書籍，四篇題材差很多。愛丁堡藝穗節喜劇《The Librarians》裡，一間搖搖欲墜的圖書館館長猝逝，接手的新館長一邊處理突擊檢查、一邊面對電線老舊、來客銳減的窘境，被拿來和經典職場喜劇《辦公室風雲》相提並論。動作驚悚片《Zip Wire》則有點荒謬——女主角是治好了肺癌的科學家，患有嚴重強迫症，卻被迫吊掛在義大利多洛米蒂山區一條老舊鋼索上，一邊對抗殺手一邊維持理智。書籍這邊，美國詩人克勞蒂亞・蘭金新作《Triage》，用回憶錄、小說與批評交織，探討面對戰爭與氣候危機這類集體創傷時，人該如何自處；娜塔莎・華特的《Feminism for a World on Fire》，則把氣候危機和全球正義運動放在一起討論，被形容是在絕望中帶來希望的作品。
voice_text: 這次的藝文評論，橫跨舞台劇、電影跟書。先講喜劇。愛丁堡藝穗節有一齣《The Librarians》，講一間搖搖欲墜的圖書館，館長突然過世，新館長一邊要應付突擊檢查，一邊要面對電線老舊、沒什麼人來的窘境，被拿來跟經典職場喜劇比。換個調性，看電影。《Zip Wire》有點荒謬，女主角是剛治好肺癌的科學家，還有嚴重強迫症，結果被迫吊在山區的鋼索上跟殺手周旋。最後看書。詩人克勞蒂亞・蘭金新書談的是，面對戰爭跟氣候危機這種集體創傷，人該怎麼自處；另一本《Feminism for a World on Fire》，把氣候危機和全球正義運動擺在一起看，評論說這本書在絕望裡，找到了一點希望。
